# Starboard: the developer pages in one file

> Starboard is a lightweight home-server dashboard and installer, with an API at /api/v1 and plug-ins that run in
> locked-down containers. This file holds the developer pages in full, for tools that read one file. The index, with a
> line for each page, is llms.txt. Made by tools/make_llms_full.py from docs/help; do not change it by hand.

---

Source: docs/help/developers/api-quickstart.md

# API quickstart

Make a key and read your first answer from Starboard's API in about 5 minutes, with curl or with Python's standard
library. A key reads, or reads and does the everyday actions of the pages, only in the areas you choose. No key
can change Starboard's settings.

## Before you begin

- Your Starboard password.
- A terminal on any computer that can open Starboard, such as the server itself. Read
  [The terminal: entering commands].
- Starboard's address. These examples use `http://192.168.1.20:8095`. Use your own.

## 1. Make a key

1. Go to **Settings**, then **Security**.
2. Find **API keys** and select **Make a key**.
3. In **Name it after what will use it**, enter a name, such as `My script`.
4. In **What it may do**, keep **Read only** unless the script must act, such as pausing downloads.
5. In **What it may read**, tick only what the script needs, or none for everything.
6. In **Ends**, choose when the key stops working.
7. Enter your Starboard password, then select **Make a key**.
8. Select **Copy**. Starboard shows the key only this once.

A key has the form `sb_read_`, six letters and numbers, another `_`, then a long secret. Keep it like a password. Read
[Authentication and keys].

## 2. Keep the key out of your commands

Put the key in an environment variable, so it is not saved in your scripts or your shell's history:

```bash
read -rs STARBOARD_KEY && export STARBOARD_KEY
```

Paste the key and press Enter. Nothing shows while you paste.

## 3. Make your first call

With curl:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/me
```

It worked when the answer gives your key's name, such as
`{"id":"a1b2c3","name":"My script","right":"read","scopes":[],...}`. The answer never includes the key itself.

With Python, using only the standard library:

```python
import json
import os
import urllib.request

BASE = "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1"
KEY = os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"]

def get(path):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + KEY})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
        return json.load(r)

for app in get("/apps")["items"]:
    print(app["name"], app["type"])
```

## 4. Read a long list a page at a time

Lists give up to 50 items by default. Ask for 1 to 200 with `limit`. When there are more, the answer's
`next_cursor` is not `null`: send it back as `cursor` to get the next page. The answer also has a `Link` header with
the next page's address.

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/downloads?limit=20"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/downloads?limit=20&cursor=bzoyMA"
```

In Python:

```python
def every(path, limit=200):
    cursor = ""
    while True:
        page = get(f"{path}?limit={limit}" + (f"&cursor={cursor}" if cursor else ""))
        yield from page["items"]
        cursor = page.get("next_cursor")
        if not cursor:
            return

for item in every("/downloads"):
    print(item.get("title"))
```

Treat a cursor as a code: do not build one yourself. A cursor Starboard did not give answers
[`bad_request`].

## 5. Ask again only when it changed

Every answer has an `ETag` header. Send it back in `If-None-Match`. When nothing has changed, Starboard answers
`304` with no body, so your script has nothing new to read.

```bash
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/status | grep -i etag
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" \
  -H 'If-None-Match: W/"3f1a9c2e7b5d8a0c4e6f"' http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/status
```

The second command prints `304` while nothing has changed. Use the `ETag` the first command printed.

Each answer's `Cache-Control` also says how many seconds it stays fresh, such as 15 seconds for `/status`. Asking
more often than that gives the same answer.

## 6. When something goes wrong

Errors are JSON problem details, with a `code` your script can check:

```json
{"type": "https://github.com/TheMightyTRex/starboard/blob/main/docs/api/errors.md#key_needed",
 "title": "Send a Starboard API key as Authorization: Bearer sb_...", "status": 401,
 "detail": "Send a Starboard API key as Authorization: Bearer sb_...", "instance": "4c1d...", "code": "key_needed"}
```

`instance` is the request's id, also in the `X-Request-Id` header. The [list of API errors]
explains each code and its fix. In Python, `urllib.request` raises `urllib.error.HTTPError` for these; read its body
with `json.load(e)`.

## Find out more

- [API reference]
- [Authentication and keys]
- [List of API errors]
- [API changelog]
- [AI prompts for developers]

# Authentication and keys

Every call to Starboard's API needs a key of its own, sent in a header. This page explains what a key is, what it
can read, how long it lasts, and the limits on it. To make one and use it, read [API quickstart].

## What a key is

- A key has the form `sb_read_a1b2c3_` or `sb_manage_a1b2c3_` and a long secret: `sb`, its right, its id (six
  letters and numbers), then the secret.
- Starboard shows the key once, when it is made. It keeps only the key's SHA-256 fingerprint, so nobody can read
  the key back, Starboard included.
- Keys are separate from signing in. A key cannot open Starboard's pages, and the browser's sign-in cannot call
  the API.
- Starboard keeps up to 50 keys. Make one for each app or script, named after it, so you can revoke one without
  stopping the others.

## Send it in the header only

Send the key in the `Authorization` header, as `Bearer`, a space, then the key:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/me
```

Starboard does not read a key anywhere else, such as in the address (`?key=...`), and refuses the call with
[`key_needed`]. Addresses end up in logs and browser history, and a header does not.

## Rights and scopes

| Right | Shown as | What it allows |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | **Read only** | Read what the API offers |
| `manage` | **Read and manage** | Read, and the everyday actions of the pages: approve or decline a request, remove or block a download, pause or resume downloads, build a Library tab again, check for container updates, run a Jellyfin job and send a test alert. With **Updates** ticked, also update Starboard, Reelix, an app or a plug-in, and roll a plug-in back (API 1.2.0) |

Every address that changes something is a `POST`, marked **Needs:** `manage` in the [API reference].
A read key gets `403` [`right_needed`] there.

No key, whatever its right, can do any of these things:

- change settings, keys or plug-in choices
- add or remove plug-ins
- change the install
- take over your apps
- restore a backup
- use Reelix's admin password
- make Starboard call an address the key gives

The one change to the install that a key can make is an update, and only with **Updates** ticked. It updates to the
version Starboard already found, with the same backup, health check and way back as the pages. The other actions stay
with a person signed in to Starboard. Read [What the API covers] for every page action and its right.

A key's scopes narrow what it reads and does. A key with no scopes reaches everything its right allows. In
**Settings**, **Security**, **What it may read**, tick only what the app or script needs. Plug-in keys only read, with
the scopes of the read permissions the person approved. Read
[The plug-in's API key].

| Scope | Shown as | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| `apps` | **Apps** | `/apps`, `/apps/{id}`, `/status`, `/health`, `/uptime`, `/app-updates`, `/numbers` and `/containers`; checking for container updates |
| `downloads` | **Downloads** | `/downloads`, `/downloads/issues`, `/transfer`, `/download-hours` and `/history`; download actions and download hours |
| `media` | **Media** | `/recent`, `/playing`, `/calendar` and `/extras`; running a Jellyfin or Audiobookshelf job |
| `library` | **Library** | `/library`, `/library/search` and `/library/status`; building a tab again |
| `requests` | **Requests** | `/requests`; approving and declining |
| `system` | **System** | `/system`, `/system/history` and `/version`; sending a test alert |
| `logs` | **Logs** | `/logs`: Starboard's log, with addresses, names and keys taken out, and `/logs/limits`. With Read and manage, also change the log limits and delete all logs. Only a key with `logs` ticked has it: a key with no scopes does not |
| `updates` | **Updates** | `/updates`, `/updates/runs` and `/updates/runs/{id}`; with **Read and manage**, starting an update and rolling a plug-in back. Only a key with `updates` ticked has it: a key with no scopes does not. API 1.2.0 |

`/api/v1/` and `/me` work with any key. `/openapi.json` needs no key. `/events` works with any key, and each event
reaches only the keys whose scopes cover it.

A key asking for something outside its scopes gets `404` [`not_found`], not `403`,
so a key cannot find out what exists beyond what it may read.

Whatever the key, the API never sends a secret. An app's API key shows only as `api_key_set`, `true` or `false`,
and the API leaves out the VPN's own internet address.

## Changes, safely

- Send the body as JSON, of up to 64 KB, such as `{"action": "pause"}`. A larger one gets `413`
  [`too_large`].
- Send an `Idempotency-Key` header, such as a new random value for each action, to make a retry safe. If you send
  the same key and value within 24 hours, you get the first answer again, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and
  Starboard does nothing twice.
- Work that takes a while, such as building a Library tab, answers `202` with `status`, the address to read to find out
  how it went.
- Starboard writes every change made with a key to the audit log, with the key's id, the address and the answer.

## Expiry

When you make a key, **Ends** sets when it stops working: **In 90 days**, **In a year** or **Never**. The list of
keys shows when each one ends. After that, it gets [`key_needed`]. Make a new one to
carry on.

## Revoke a key

Go to **Settings**, then **Security**, then **API keys**, and select **Revoke** beside the key. Anything using it
stops working at once. Changing your password or signing out everywhere does not stop a key: revoke it.

The list shows when each key was last used, to the nearest minute, so you can find keys nothing uses any more.

## Rate limits

- Each key can make up to 120 requests a minute. Past that, the answer is `429`
  [`rate_limited`], with `Retry-After`: the seconds to wait.
- Every answer has a `RateLimit` header saying how many requests are left, such as `"per-key";r=118;t=0`, and a
  `RateLimit-Policy` header, `"per-key";q=120;w=60`.
- Wrong keys count towards the same lockout as wrong passwords, for each address. Too many, and the address gets
  `429` [`too_many_attempts`] for 15 minutes.

Every request counts, a `304` included. To stay well inside the limit, ask no more often than the answer's
`Cache-Control` says it stays fresh. Use `If-None-Match` with the last `ETag`, so an answer that has not changed
has no body to read. Read [API quickstart].

## The audit log

Starboard writes a line to its audit log, `data/logs/audit.jsonl`, in these cases:

- each time someone makes or revokes a key;
- each time a key changes something (`api_write`, with the key's id, the address and the answer's status);
- each time Starboard refuses a wrong key, with the address it came from;
- each time someone adds, updates, rolls back, activates or removes a plug-in;
- each sign-in step beyond the password: the two-step code activated or off, a code or recovery code used or refused,
  single sign-on set up, tested, activated or off, and each sign-in it allowed or refused, with the address it came
  from (`totp_enabled`, `sign_in_code_ok`, `sign_in_code_failed`, `sign_in_recovery_code_used`, `sso_configured`,
  `sign_in_sso`, `sso_refused` and the like).

The log never holds a key or a password. It keeps 5 files of about 1 MB each, and counts towards the log limits in
Settings, General, Backup/Logs. Its older files go with the oldest days, and Delete all logs empties it (the
delete itself is its next line).

## The calendar address is not a key

The Coming up page makes an address for calendar apps, `/calendar.ics?token=sbcal_...`, because a calendar app
cannot send a header. Its token is not an API key:

- It opens that one iCalendar file and nothing else. The API, the pages and the sign-in never accept it, and an API
  key or a signed-in browser cannot open the file.
- There is one at a time. Starboard keeps only its SHA-256 fingerprint and shows it once; a new one stops the old
  one at once.
- A refused token counts towards the same lockout per address as a refused key. A good one shares the limit of 120
  a minute, and the file is kept for 15 minutes, so asking more often reads nothing new.
- Making or stopping it is written to the audit log as `calendar_address_made` or `calendar_address_stopped`, and a
  refused one as `calendar_refused`.

## Keep keys safe

- Treat a key like a password. Keep it in an environment variable or a file only you can read, not in your code.
- Do not paste a key into a chat, a forum or an AI assistant. If one gets out, revoke it and make another.
- Starboard's API answers over plain `http` on your home network. To use it away from home, read
  [Use Starboard away from home safely].

## Find out more

- [API quickstart]
- [API reference]
- [What the API covers]
- [Connect an AI assistant]

- [Make an API key and use Starboard's API]
- [How Starboard keeps your server safe]

# MCP tools

Starboard answers the Model Context Protocol (MCP) at `POST /api/v1/mcp`, from API 1.7.0. An AI assistant connects
with a **Read only** API key and gets tools that read the media server through the same routes as `/api/v1`. This page
describes the transport, the rules and each tool. For setting it up as an owner, read
[Let an AI assistant answer questions about your server].

## The transport

- **Streamable HTTP, without streams.** Send one JSON-RPC 2.0 message as the body of a `POST`, with
  `Content-Type: application/json`. A request gets one `application/json` answer. Starboard never answers with
  `text/event-stream` and never keeps a connection open, so `GET /api/v1/mcp` answers `405`.
- **Methods:** `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`. Anything else answers the JSON-RPC error `-32601`.
- **Notifications** such as `notifications/initialized` and `notifications/cancelled`, which have no `id`, get `202`
  and no body.
- **No batches.** A JSON array answers `400` with the JSON-RPC error `-32600`. Not JSON at all answers `400` with
  `-32700`.
- **No session.** Starboard gives no `Mcp-Session-Id`: each request stands on its own, so a restart of Starboard does
  not break the assistant's connection.
- **Versions:** `2025-06-18` and `2025-03-26`. `initialize` agrees the version the client asks for when Starboard
  has it, or else the newest. After that, a client may send `MCP-Protocol-Version`; a version Starboard does not
  speak answers `400 bad_request`.
- **Size:** a message of up to 64 KB (`413 too_large`).

## The rules

| Rule | What happens otherwise |
|---|---|
| The owner has activated **Let AI assistants connect** in Settings, Security, API keys. | `403` [`mcp_off`] |
| `Authorization: Bearer` and a key that works. Refused keys count towards the lockout for the address. | `401` [`key_needed`] |
| The key is **Read only**. | `403` [`read_key_needed`] |
| No `Origin` header, or one for the same address as `Host`. | `403` [`origin_refused`] |
| A name Starboard answers to, as for every request. | `421` |
| Up to 120 requests a minute for each key, shared with the rest of the API. | `429` [`rate_limited`] |

`tools/list` gives only the tools whose scope the key has. A key with no scopes has every tool here, as none needs
**Logs** or **Updates**. Calling a tool the key does not have answers the JSON-RPC error `-32602`, the same as a tool
that does not exist.

Each `tools/call` writes one line to the audit log, `mcp_call`, with the key's id, the tool's name and whether it
worked. The arguments are not written.

## Answers from a tool

Each tool says `readOnlyHint: true` and changes nothing. A tool that worked answers `isError: false`, with the answer
twice: as `structuredContent`, which matches the tool's `outputSchema`, and as JSON text in `content`. A tool that
ran but could not answer, for example because Reelix is not added or an app did not answer, gives `isError: true`
and the reason as text. Wrong arguments answer the JSON-RPC error `-32602`, with what was wrong.

`limit` is from 1 to 50 and 20 when left out. `more` is `true` when there were more than `limit`. Each list holds
the same objects as the route it reads, with secrets taken out.

## The tools

| Tool | Scope | Arguments | Gives back | Reads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `search_library` | `library` | `query` (1 to 120 letters, required), `limit` | `items`, `more` | `GET /api/v1/library/search` |
| `recently_added` | `media` | `limit` | `items`, `more` | `GET /api/v1/recent` |
| `coming_up` | `media` | `month` (such as `2026-11`), `limit` | `items`, `more`, `errors` | `GET /api/v1/calendar` |
| `now_playing` | `media` | none | `configured`, `items` | `GET /api/v1/playing` |
| `downloads_in_progress` | `downloads` | `limit` | `items`, `more`, `errors` | `GET /api/v1/downloads` |
| `download_problems` | `downloads` | `limit` | `count`, `items`, `errors` | `GET /api/v1/downloads/issues` |
| `requests` | `requests` | `pending_only` (true or false), `limit` | `items`, `more`, `configured`, `pending` | `GET /api/v1/requests` |
| `app_health` | `apps` | none | `apps`, `problems`, `errors` | `GET /api/v1/status` and `GET /api/v1/health` |
| `disk_space` | `system` | none | `disks` | `GET /api/v1/system` |

- `errors` lists the apps that did not answer, so a partial answer says what is missing.
- `download_problems` gives the same items as `GET /api/v1/downloads/issues`, without its Markdown.
- `app_health`: `apps` is whether each app answers; `problems` is what the apps report about themselves.
- `disk_space`: each disk has `label`, `total`, `used` and `free` in bytes, or `missing: true`.

## An example

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$STARBOARD_URL/api/v1/mcp" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "disk_space", "arguments": {}}}'
```

```json
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": {
  "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "{\"disks\":[{\"label\":\"Media\",\"total\":4000000000000,\"used\":2500000000000,\"free\":1500000000000}]}"}],
  "structuredContent": {"disks": [{"label": "Media", "total": 4000000000000, "used": 2500000000000, "free": 1500000000000}]},
  "isError": false}}
```

## What is left for later

Tools that change something, such as approving a request or pausing downloads, are not offered. When they come,
each will wait for the owner to approve it in Starboard's page first, and need its own decision.

## Find out more

- [Let an AI assistant answer questions about your server]
- [Authentication and keys]
- [API reference: POST /api/v1/mcp]

# API reference

This page is made from Starboard's API description, `starboard/openapi.json` (version 1.10.0), by `tools/make_api_reference.py`. It lists every address in version 1 of the API.

- Every address starts with `/api/v1` on your Starboard, such as `http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/apps`.
- Every request except the description itself needs a key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer` and the key. Addresses that change something are `POST` and need a key made with **Read and manage**. Read [Authentication and keys].
- The examples read the key from `STARBOARD_KEY`. Set it first, such as `export STARBOARD_KEY=sb_read_...`.
- Lists take `limit` and `cursor`, and every answer has an `ETag`. Read [API quickstart].
- Errors are problem details (RFC 9457), each explained in the [list of API errors].
- The same description is on your Starboard at `/api/v1/openapi.json`, for tools that read OpenAPI.

## About

### GET /api/v1/

The API's version, Starboard's version and links.

- **Key:** any key.
- **Fresh for:** 3600 seconds (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600`).
- **Operation id:** `getRoot`.

The answer:

- [Root].

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/",
                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"]})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

### GET /api/v1/me

The key you are using: its name, right and scopes.

- **Key:** any key.
- **Fresh for:** 60 seconds (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=60`).
- **Operation id:** `getMe`.

The answer:

- [Key].

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/me"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/me",
                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"]})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

### GET /api/v1/openapi.json

This description.

- **Key:** none needed.
- **Operation id:** `getOpenApi`.

The answer:

- The OpenAPI 3.1 description.

Example:

```bash
curl -s "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/openapi.json"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/openapi.json")
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

## Apps

### GET /api/v1/apps

The apps on the dashboard.

- **Key:** any key whose scopes are empty or include `apps` (your apps and their status). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Fresh for:** 60 seconds (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=60`).
- **Operation id:** `listApps`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | How many to give back; 1 to 200, 50 if left out. |
| `cursor` | query | The next_cursor of the previous answer. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | a list of [App] | yes |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | yes |

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`], when `limit` or `cursor` is wrong.
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/apps"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/apps",
                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"]})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

### GET /api/v1/apps/{id}

One app.

- **Key:** any key whose scopes are empty or include `apps` (your apps and their status). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Fresh for:** 60 seconds (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=60`).
- **Operation id:** `getApp`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | text. Required. |

The answer:

- [App].

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **404:** [`not_found`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/apps/sonarr"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/apps/sonarr",
                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"]})
```

### GET /api/v1/status

Whether each app answers, checked every 15 seconds at most.

- **Key:** any key whose scopes are empty or include `apps` (your apps and their status). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Fresh for:** 15 seconds (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=15`).
- **Operation id:** `listStatus`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | How many to give back; 1 to 200, 50 if left out. |
| `cursor` | query | The next_cursor of the previous answer. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | a list of an object (its fields vary) | yes |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | yes |

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`], when `limit` or `cursor` is wrong.
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

### POST /api/v1/containers/check

Check for newer images of the apps' containers now.

- **Key:** a key made with Read and manage whose scopes are empty or include `apps` (your apps and their status). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Needs:** `manage`. A read key gets `403 right_needed`. Send a JSON body; `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry safe.
- **Operation id:** `checkContainers`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Send the same value again to get the first answer back without doing it twice. Kept for 24 hours. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `available` | true or false | yes |
| `checked_at` | a number or null | no |
| `restored` | true or false | no |
| `items` | a list of an object (its fields vary) | yes |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | no |

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`].
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **403:** [`right_needed`].
- **404:** [`not_found`].
- **413:** [`too_large`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}' "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/containers/check"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/containers/check", method="POST", data=b'{}',
                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"],
                                      "Content-Type": "application/json"})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

### POST /api/v1/download-hours

Resume or pause downloads until the next change of the hours, or follow the hours again.

- **Key:** a key made with Read and manage whose scopes are empty or include `downloads` (downloads, download hours and history). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Needs:** `manage`. A read key gets `403 right_needed`. Send a JSON body; `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry safe.
- **Operation id:** `actOnDownloadHours`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Send the same value again to get the first answer back without doing it twice. Kept for 24 hours. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | true or false | yes |
| `start` | a whole number | no |
| `end` | a whole number | no |
| `mode` | one of `run`, `pause` | no |
| `reason` | text | no |
| `next_change` | text | no |
| `clients` | a list of text | no |
| `now` | a list of an object (its fields vary) | no |
| `errors` | a list of an object (its fields vary) | no |

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`].
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **403:** [`right_needed`].
- **404:** [`not_found`].
- **413:** [`too_large`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"action": "resume"}' "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/download-hours"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/download-hours", method="POST", data=b'{"action": "resume"}',
                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"],
                                      "Content-Type": "application/json"})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

- **413:** [`too_large`].

### GET /api/v1/downloads/issues

Every download that needs attention or failed, with its details, and as Markdown for an AI helper.

Each app's queue is asked once when you call this (at most every 10 seconds), never on a timer. markdown starts with a short prompt telling an AI helper what to do, then one section for each download. Keys, passwords, tokens, private addresses and full download addresses are taken out; paths are only those in media and download folders.

- **Key:** any key whose scopes are empty or include `downloads` (downloads, download hours and history). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Fresh for:** 10 seconds (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=10`).
- **Operation id:** `listDownloadIssues`.

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `generated_at` | text (date-time) | yes |
| `count` | a whole number | yes |
| `apps_asked` | a whole number | yes |
| `items` | a list of [DownloadIssue] | yes |
| `errors` | a list of an object (its fields vary) | yes |
| `markdown` | text | yes |

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/downloads/issues"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/downloads/issues",
                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"]})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | How many to give back; 1 to 200, 50 if left out. |
| `cursor` | query | The next_cursor of the previous answer. |
| `month` | query | A month, such as 2026-11, with a week either side. Without it, from yesterday for the days set in Settings, General. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | a list of an object (its fields vary) | yes |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | yes |
| `errors` | a list of an object (its fields vary) | no |

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`].
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/calendar"
```

```python

                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"]})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

### GET /api/v1/logs/limits

How long Starboard keeps its logs, the most they may take, and what they take now.

Only for keys that ticked Logs: a key with no scopes does not have them. Whichever limit comes first removes the oldest days: when a new day starts, when the limits change and when the size written passes the limit. They cover Starboard's own log (with its jobs, updates and plug-ins' lines), the API's audit log and the last Starboard update's log. apps is the apps' own limit, read from Docker.

- **Key:** any key whose scopes include `logs` (the logs, only when ticked). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Fresh for:** 30 seconds (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=30`).
- **Operation id:** `getLogLimits`.

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `keep_days` | one of `7`, `14`, `30`, `60`, `90`, `180`, `365` | yes |
| `max_mb` | one of `10`, `25`, `50`, `100`, `250`, `500` | yes |
| `show_lines` | one of `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`, `1000` | no |
| `alerts_only` | true or false | no |
| `keep_days_choices` | a list of a whole number | yes |
| `show_lines_choices` | a list of a whole number | no |
| `max_mb_choices` | a list of a whole number | yes |
| `summary` | an object | yes |
| `covers` | a list of text | yes |
| `apps` | an object | no |
| `removed` | a whole number | no |
| `freed` | a whole number | no |

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/logs/limits"
```

```python

                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"]})
```
```python
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

### POST /api/v1/logs/delete

Delete all logs.

Only for keys that ticked Logs: a key with no scopes does not have them. Every log the limits cover goes, apart from today's file and the audit log, which are emptied, and the last update's log while an update runs. Cannot be undone. The first new line says the key deleted them; this write is in the audit log too. The apps' own logs (Docker's) are not touched.

- **Key:** a key made with Read and manage whose scopes include `logs` (the logs, only when ticked). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Needs:** `manage`. A read key gets `403 right_needed`. Send a JSON body; `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry safe.
- **Operation id:** `deleteLogs`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Send the same value again to get the first answer back without doing it twice. Kept for 24 hours. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `removed` | a whole number | yes |
| `emptied` | a whole number | yes |
| `freed` | a whole number | yes |
| `summary` | an object | yes |

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`].
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **403:** [`right_needed`].
- **404:** [`not_found`].
- **413:** [`too_large`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"confirm": "example"}' "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/logs/delete"
```

```python

                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"],
                                      "Content-Type": "application/json"})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | text. Required. |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Send the same value again to get the first answer back without doing it twice. Kept for 24 hours. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | true or false | yes |

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`].
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **403:** [`right_needed`].
- **404:** [`not_found`].
- **413:** [`too_large`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].
- **502:** [`app_failed`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}' "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/requests/123/approve"
```

## Events

### GET /api/v1/events

Events as they happen, as Server-Sent Events.

A text/event-stream. Each event is CloudEvents-shaped JSON: specversion, id, type (such as starboard.app.down), source, time and data. A key hears only the events its scopes cover. Send Last-Event-ID to resume. Up to 8 streams at once; each closes after an hour.

- **Key:** any key.
- **Operation id:** `streamEvents`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Last-Event-ID` | header | The id of the last event you read. |

The answer:

- The stream.

Errors:

- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].
- **503:** [`too_many_streams`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/events"
```

```python
    print(json.load(r))
```

## Updates

### GET /api/v1/updates

What can be updated: Starboard, Reelix, the other apps and the plug-ins.

Only for keys that ticked Updates: a key with no scopes does not have them. From what Starboard already knows (its release check, the last check for app updates and the catalogues it has read): nothing is fetched to answer. running is the update running now, if any.

- **Key:** any key whose scopes include `updates` (updates, only when ticked). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Fresh for:** 30 seconds (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=30`).
- **Operation id:** `listUpdates`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | How many to give back; 1 to 200, 50 if left out. |
| `cursor` | query | The next_cursor of the previous answer. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | a list of [UpdateTarget] | yes |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | yes |
| `running` | [UpdateRun] or null | no |

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`], when `limit` or `cursor` is wrong.
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:



### POST /api/v1/updates

Start an update to the newest version Starboard knows.

Only for keys that ticked Updates: a key with no scopes does not have them. One update runs at a time. Each has the same backup, health check and way back as on the pages: Starboard runs update.sh; Reelix and the other apps keep their old image until the new one is healthy; a plug-in runs its before step, moves its settings, waits for its health check and goes back by itself if it fails. Never from an address: only the version Starboard already found.

- **Key:** a key made with Read and manage whose scopes include `updates` (updates, only when ticked). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Needs:** `manage`. A read key gets `403 right_needed`. Send a JSON body; `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry safe.
- **Operation id:** `startUpdate`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Send the same value again to get the first answer back without doing it twice. Kept for 24 hours. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `accepted` | true or false | yes |
| `run` | [UpdateRun] | yes |
| `status` | text | yes |

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`].
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **403:** [`right_needed`].
- **404:** [`not_found`].
- **409:** [`update_running`], [`cannot_update`].
- **413:** [`too_large`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].
- **502:** [`app_failed`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"target": "example"}' "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/updates"
```

```python

    print(json.load(r))
```

### GET /api/v1/updates/all

What Install all updates would do now, in order, and what is held back.

Only for keys that ticked Updates: a key with no scopes does not have them. items run one at a time, in this order: the other apps, Jellyfin's plug-ins, Starboard's plug-ins, Reelix, then Jellyfin restarts once (never while someone is watching), then Starboard last. held lists what always waits for you: a plug-in asking for new permissions or that comes as a zip file, a new major version, and anything Starboard cannot update here. Reads each waiting plug-in's new manifest from its catalogue (kept 10 minutes). count does not include Jellyfin's plug-ins, whose new versions only Jellyfin knows.

- **Key:** any key whose scopes include `updates` (updates, only when ticked). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Fresh for:** 60 seconds (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=60`).
- **Operation id:** `planAllUpdates`.

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | a list of an object | yes |
| `held` | a list of an object | yes |
| `count` | a whole number | yes |

Other answers:

- **304:** Not changed since the ETag sent in If-None-Match.

Errors:

- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].


### POST /api/v1/updates/all

Install all updates: every waiting update as one batch.

Only for keys that ticked Updates: a key with no scopes does not have them. One at a time, never in parallel, each with its own backup, health check and way back. One that fails goes back by itself and the rest carry on. Answers 409 update_running while another update runs, and 409 cannot_update when nothing is waiting or everything waiting is held back.

- **Key:** a key made with Read and manage whose scopes include `updates` (updates, only when ticked). A key without it gets `404 not_found`.
- **Needs:** `manage`. A read key gets `403 right_needed`. Send a JSON body; `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry safe.
- **Operation id:** `startAllUpdates`.

| `run` | [UpdateRun] | yes |
| `status` | text | yes |

- **400:** [`bad_request`].
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **403:** [`right_needed`].
- **404:** [`not_found`].
- **409:** [`update_running`], [`cannot_update`].
- **413:** [`too_large`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].


## AI assistants

### POST /api/v1/mcp

AI assistants: the Model Context Protocol, read-only tools about the media server.

The MCP Streamable HTTP transport: send one JSON-RPC 2.0 message as JSON (no batches) and get one JSON answer, never a stream. It takes initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call; notifications, with no id, get 202 and no body. Off until the owner activates AI assistants in Settings, Security, API keys (403 mcp_off). Only a Read only key (403 read_key_needed). tools/list gives the tools the key's scopes cover: search_library (library), recently_added, coming_up and now_playing (media), downloads_in_progress and download_problems (downloads), requests (requests), app_health (apps) and disk_space (system). Each reads the same as its /api/v1 route and changes nothing. Each tools/call is written to the audit log. An Origin header from another site is refused (403 origin_refused). MCP versions 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26; send MCP-Protocol-Version after initialize.

- **Key:** a Read only key.
- **Operation id:** `mcp`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `MCP-Protocol-Version` | header | The version initialize agreed. |

The answer:

- [JsonRpcResponse].

Other answers:

- **202:** A notification was taken. No body.

Errors:

- **400:** Not JSON, or not one JSON-RPC 2.0 message (a JSON-RPC error), or an MCP version Starboard does not speak (a problem).
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **403:** [`mcp_off`], [`read_key_needed`], [`origin_refused`].
- **405:** [`method_not_allowed`].
- **413:** [`too_large`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list"}' "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/mcp"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/mcp", method="POST", data=b'{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list"}',
                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"],
                                      "Content-Type": "application/json"})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

## Plug-ins

### POST /api/v1/plugin/alerts

A plug-in raises or clears one of its alerts, sent through Starboard's own alerts.

Only the plug-in's own key, while the plug-in is active and its approved permissions include alerts:send: any other key gets 404 not_found. The one write a plug-in's read-only key may do. An alert goes out once until it is cleared, to where Starboard sends its own (ntfy, Gotify or a webhook), as the alert.raised and alert.cleared events and in the log, and only while alerts are on. Up to 30 new alerts an hour for each plug-in (429 rate_limited with Retry-After); raising one that is already raised does not count.

- **Key:** only a plug-in's own key, while the plug-in is active and its approved permissions include `alerts:send`. Any other key gets `404 not_found`.
- **Operation id:** `sendPluginAlert`.

Parameters:

| Name | In | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Send the same value again to get the first answer back without doing it twice. Kept for 24 hours. |

The answer:

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | true or false | yes |
| `sent` | true or false | yes |

Errors:

- **400:** [`bad_request`].
- **401:** [`key_needed`].
- **404:** [`not_found`].
- **413:** [`too_large`].
- **429:** [`too_many_attempts`], [`rate_limited`].

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STARBOARD_KEY" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key": "check-router", "state": "raised", "title": "Router is not answering", "message": "Ping: no answer for 3 checks in a row.", "level": "problem"}' "http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/plugin/alerts"
```

```python
import json, os, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request("http://192.168.1.20:8095/api/v1/plugin/alerts", method="POST", data=b'{"key": "check-router", "state": "raised", "title": "Router is not answering", "message": "Ping: no answer for 3 checks in a row.", "level": "problem"}',
                             headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["STARBOARD_KEY"],
                                      "Content-Type": "application/json"})
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
    print(json.load(r))
```

## Objects

The named objects the answers use.

### App

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | yes |
| `name` | text | yes |
| `type` | text | yes |
| `group` | text | yes |
| `enabled` | true or false | yes |
| `url` | text | yes |
| `api_key_set` | true or false | yes |

### DownloadIssue

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `app` | text | yes |
| `app_id` | text | yes |
| `app_type` | one of `sonarr`, `radarr`, `lidarr`, `readarr`, `reelix` | yes |
| `reelix` | true or false | yes |
| `kind` | text | yes |
| `what` | text | yes |
| `title` | text | yes |
| `status` | one of `Needs attention`, `Failed` | yes |
| `app_state` | an object (its fields vary) | yes |
| `messages` | a list of text | yes |
| `size` | a number | yes |
| `progress` | a number | yes |
| `time_left` | text | yes |
| `added` | text | yes |
| `age` | text | yes |
| `indexer` | text | yes |
| `protocol` | text | yes |
| `quality` | text | yes |
| `download_client` | text | yes |
| `download_client_ids` | an object (its fields vary) | yes |
| `paths` | an object (its fields vary) | yes |
| `ids` | an object (its fields vary) | yes |
| `can_manual_import` | true or false | no |
| `tried` | a list of an object | yes |

### JsonRpcResponse

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | one of `2.0` | yes |
| `id` | text or a whole number or null | yes |
| `result` | an object (its fields vary) | no |
| `error` | an object | no |

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | yes |
| `name` | text | yes |

| `expires_at` | text (date-time) or null | no |
| `last_used_at` | text (date-time) or null | no |
| `prefix` | text | yes |

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `api_version` | text | yes |
| `starboard_version` | text | yes |

| Field | What it is | Always there |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | yes |
| `target` | text | yes |
| `kind` | one of `starboard`, `reelix`, `app`, `plugin`, `jellyfin-plugins`, `batch` | yes |
| `name` | text | yes |
| `action` | one of `update`, `rollback` | yes |
| `from` | text | yes |
| `to` | text | yes |
| `by` | text | yes |
| `state` | one of `running`, `updated`, `up-to-date`, `went-back`, `rolled-back`, `refused`, `failed`, `some-updated` | yes |
| `said` | text | yes |
| `started_at` | text (date-time) | yes |
| `finished_at` | text (date-time) or null | no |
| `steps` | a list of an object | yes |
